news.text: The Bills head coach told reporters on Tuesday that he was not concerned by the quarterback's quiet outing in New York, describing the issues as protection-related rather than anything physical, and said he expects a normal week of preparation.
Buffalo's quarterback has been managing a shoulder problem and was limited in practice on Wednesday, according to a team source.
A beat writer noted that Buffalo's quarterback has been pressured on 34 percent of his dropbacks through the first two weeks, the eighth-highest rate in the league.
Buffalo listed linebacker Matt Milano as out for Thursday's game with a pectoral injury, and defensive tackle Ed Oliver as out with an ankle injury.
